events.title: French protectorate and the Franco-Tahitian War
hints: An unwelcome protectorate was imposed on a queen in 1842.
The expulsion of a British missionary-consul, George Pritchard, caused a diplomatic row.
Fighting ended with a French victory in 1847.
events.summary: France imposed a protectorate over Queen Pomare IV in 1842 after intrigues involving missionaries. The arrest and expulsion of the British consul George Pritchard sparked an international row, and the Franco-Tahitian War of 1844 to 1847 ended with French control.

events.title: Annexation and the French Establishments in Oceania
hints: The last Pomare king ceded his realm in June 1880.
Other island groups were annexed over the next two decades.
The colony was called the French Establishments in Oceania.
events.summary: In June 1880 King Pomare V ceded Tahiti to France, which annexed the other island groups through the 1880s and 1890s. The colony, called the French Establishments in Oceania, became an overseas territory in 1946.

events.title: Makatea phosphate mining
hints: A raised coral island was mined for fertiliser for nearly sixty years.
A French company ran mining, railways and a port.
It closed in 1966, just as nuclear testing began.
events.summary: From 1908 to 1966 a French company mined phosphate on Makatea atoll for use as fertiliser, building railways and a port and employing workers from across the territory. The mine closed in 1966, leaving the atoll almost depopulated.

events.title: French nuclear testing
hints: A nuclear test centre was moved from the Algerian desert to the ocean after 1962.
Nearly two hundred tests took place at two atolls over three decades.
The final series in 1995 and 1996 prompted riots and global protest.
events.summary: From 1966 to 1996 France carried out 193 nuclear tests at Moruroa and Fangataufa atolls, 46 of them atmospheric until 1974. The tests raised long-term health and environmental concerns, and the 1995 to 1996 series triggered protests worldwide.
